_note: Frozen content for design review. Teaching family — the diagrams are the design. Three body kinds rotate: a column chart, a process flow and a comparison table, each closing on one lime takeaway.
brief: How a retrieval system actually gets built, and where it goes wrong

slots.eyebrow: A working system, not a diagram of one
slots.lede: Six stages, in the order they break. The interesting failures are all in the first three, which is where nobody looks.
slots.barLbl1: What the data has to look like first
slots.barLbl2: How chunking decides what can be found
slots.barLbl3: Why the retrieval step is the whole system
slots.barLbl4: Choosing a model by fit, not by size
slots.barLbl5: What breaks once real users arrive

slots.title: Answer quality tracks
slots.subtitle: The same pipeline, the same model, five different states of the underlying documents.
slots.insightText: Fixing the documents moved it fifty points. Upgrading the model moved it two.

slots.title: Four steps, and only one of them
slots.subtitle: Everything that determines whether an answer is any good happens before generation.
slots.node1Sub: Users ask badly. Expanding the query is cheaper than any model upgrade.
slots.node2Sub: Cast wide here. Recall is recoverable later; a missed document never is.
slots.node3Sub: The step teams skip. It is where precision actually comes from.
slots.node4Sub: By this point the model is mostly formatting what it was handed.
slots.insightText: If the right document was not retrieved, no model can recover it.

slots.title: How you cut the documents decides
slots.subtitle: Same corpus, same retriever, four splitting strategies measured on the same question set.
slots.insightText: Whole documents find everything and answer nothing. Structure beats size.

slots.title: Bigger stops paying
slots.subtitle: Accuracy on the same grounded task, plotted against cost per thousand answers.
slots.insightText: A mid model with reranking matched the largest one at a fraction of the cost.

slots.title: Every failure in production
slots.subtitle: Four things that only appear once people who did not build it start asking questions.
slots.node1Sub: The system answers confidently from the nearest document it has.
slots.node2Sub: Nothing fails loudly. Answers just quietly describe last quarter.
slots.node3Sub: Whichever ranks higher wins, which is not the same as being right.
slots.node4Sub: Without the retrieved passages logged, every complaint is unfalsifiable.
slots.insightText: Log what was retrieved, not just what was said. It is the only debuggable part.

slots.title: Most of this is unnecessary
slots.subtitle: What the same question set costs to answer well, by how much material there actually is.
slots.insightText: Under fifty pages, the whole pipeline loses to pasting the documents in.

slots.eyebrow: Before you build any of it
slots.ctaBody: Take thirty real questions, check whether the right passage comes back at all, and only then argue about models.
slots.recap1: Fix the documents before the pipeline
slots.recap2: Cut by structure, never by character count
slots.recap3: Rerank — it is the cheapest accuracy there is
slots.recap4: Log the passages or you cannot debug it
